result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=with, B=without): Both answers replace the grid with a queue ordered by need, show the specific question each stuck agent is asking, group shared causes and treat the over-$25k sign-off as its own approval lane. A wins because it adds group pause and stop controls that show how many agents will be affected, and it says sign-offs must never be batched. B offers a 'take over' action and a banner for problems hitting many agents, but no way to pause agents or the fleet. | pass 2 (A=without, B=with): Both answers make a grouped, triaged queue the main surface, show the specific ask for each stuck agent, and treat the over-$25k sign-off as its own lane rather than an error. B is better on intervention control: it offers group pause and stop with a confirmation count, keeps pause separate from stop, and gives an unattended-queue escalation to a named backup. A has a 'take over' action but no fleet-wide or group pause. B also adds that each sign-off is decided and recorded on its own, never batched, and lets the supervisor exclude a claim that doesn't fit from a group decision.
